items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Markets face an "uncomfortable sweet spot" characterized by strong AI-driven growth alongside high structural deficits, debt leverage, and rising yields, with experts weighing risks of deceleration, a crowded AI capex cycle, and the upcoming midterm elections.

## Economic Outlook & Fiscal Policy
* **Robert Kaplan on US Growth Dynamics:** 
  * The economy is super strong in AI-related and defense sectors, but sluggish in housing, autos, and serving lower-middle-income consumers.
  * Inflation is largely structural rather than cyclical, driven heavily by energy costs like elevated diesel prices embedded across 50 items.
  * Recommends the Fed debate how much current inflation is supply-driven versus demand-driven rather than acting as if the economy is simply overheating.
* **Fiscal Deficits & Government Leverage:**
  * Governments globally are highly leveraged in the aftermath of COVID, pushing the Treasury curve to act poorly as a cyclical diversifier.
  * **Robert Kaplan's Reform Menu:** Advocates addressing long-term debt through immigration reform (bringing in 1–2 million workers annually to fill open jobs), balanced regulation, reinstituted embedded cost management, and entitlement reform.
  * Notes that the 2026 budget deficit miss included a **$250 billion** entitlement surprise heading north and **$100 billion** in interest expense.
* **Colin Graham on Nominal Growth & Global Divergence:**
  * High nominal GDP growth in the US has allowed sectors like UPS and consumers to generate good earnings, but fiscal stimulus will likely decline next year and deflate nominal GDP.
  * Europe—specifically France—lacks the US growth buffer, suffering from tight ECB monetary conditions and an acute energy shock where economic growth cannot cover interest costs.

## AI Infrastructure Boom & Financial Stability Risks
* **Gary Gensler on Financial and Technology Risks:**
  * The AI infrastructure boom has raised over **$500 billion** in new debt this year, alongside a **$63 billion** Broadcom deal, pushing total new debt near **$600 billion**.
  * Warns that the insurance sector is increasingly holding this debt through private credit or direct exposure.
  * Highlights off-balance-sheet guarantees written into data centers by Broadcom, NVIDIA, and AMD via special purpose vehicles that rival past financial engineering.
* **Technology Obsolescence & Corporate Adoption:**
  * **Gary Gensler:** Expresses uncertainty regarding the depreciation and obsolescence of memory and processor chips, noting that chips built in 2026 may lose significant value by **2032** due to rapid scaling and technological advances.
  * **Robert Kaplan:** Estimates that out of **2% real GDP growth**, roughly half may be related to AI, warning that a roll-over in this narrow adoption wave could severely impact the broader economy.

## Equity Markets & Multi-Asset Strategy
* **Mike Wilson on S&P 500 Valuations and Corrections:**
  * The market has experienced a significant correction under the surface since June, which is currently **80-90% done** (in the 9th inning).
  * The S&P 500 multiple has compressed by nearly **20%** from a year ago (down from **23x** to **18-19x** earnings), successfully discounting growth deceleration.
  * Advises staying on board with quality factors and leaders rather than just the Magnificent 7, noting that strong underlying earnings growth will face tougher comps next year.
* **Colin Graham on Asset Allocation:**
  * Fixed income offers limited upside with a **5%** return compared to equities delivering **20%** from earnings growth.
  * Currency dynamics show a stronger dollar concentrates growth in the US while keeping a floor on market volatility.

## Workplace Culture & Human Capital
* **In-Office Mandates vs. Remote Work:**
  * **Robert Kaplan:** Argues that remote work causes training, mentoring, coaching, and relationship-building skills to atrophy, making in-person gathering at firms like Goldman Sachs essential for professional development.
  * **Gary Gensler:** Notes that while 98% of MIT students and faculty utilize AI, users must actively train their cognitive faculties to avoid "cognitive decline" from offloading critical thinking entirely to automated tools.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Robert Kaplan:** The Fed should skip a rate cut/hike today and raise rates deliberately, acknowledging that the data leaves much unknown.
* **Robert Kaplan:** The AI adoption phase will fundamentally change the employment mix, resulting in fewer programmers and more client-facing, relationship-building personnel.
* **Gary Gensler:** The Federal Reserve might pause its rate path after a potential December move.
* **Mike Wilson:** The current under-the-surface equity correction is in its 9th inning and will conclude with clearing events like the midterm elections, allowing the bull market to advance into 2027.

## Notable Quotes
> "If I thought this was a cyclical overheating, I’d say, 'Let’s get moving faster.' But... the impact of raising too far or too fast may be to slow already sluggish parts of the economy, and it may not make a dent in inflation."
> — Robert Kaplan

> "We've raised over 500 billion dollars of new debt this year and then you add this Broadcom 63 billion. So we're pushing 600 billion. And who holds it? I think it's insurance sector I worry about that's picked up a lot of holding of debt through private credit or just directly."
> — Gary Gensler

> "Don't tell me that the market isn't paying attention. It is. The question is, is that enough of a discount? I think the multiple now is cheap enough to, to basically feel comfortable that it's discounted a lot of these risks."
> — Mike Wilson

items.title: Property Play: How Green Financing Is Reshaping Real Estate
items.summary: C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) financing provides commercial real estate owners with long-term, fixed-rate capital tied to energy efficiency and climate resilience that runs with the land, helping borrowers navigate a $1 trillion debt maturity wall and rising interest rates.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) financing provides commercial real estate owners with long-term, fixed-rate capital tied to energy efficiency and climate resilience that runs with the land, helping borrowers navigate a $1 trillion debt maturity wall and rising interest rates.

## What is C-PACE Financing?
* **Definition and Mechanism:** **C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy)** is a state-level policy enabling commercial property owners to create a voluntary special tax assessment district on their own property to secure long-term financing for energy efficiency, solar panels, and extreme weather resiliency upgrades.
* **Deal Flexibility:** **Flexible Capital Stack Integration:** The financing can be used to take out construction financing on recently completed upgrades, fund new property construction (securing more capital by outperforming energy code), or retrofit existing properties.
* **Senior Security:** **Runs with the Land:** C-PACE assessments survive bankruptcies and foreclosures, staying attached to the property even if sold, which provides the long-dated, highly secure assets sought by institutional investors.

## Company Growth & Scale (Nuveen Green Capital)
* **AUM Expansion:** **$7 Billion AUM:** Nuveen Green Capital grew from **$300 million** in assets under management at the time of its 2021 acquisition by Nuveen up to **$7 billion** to date.
* **Geographic Reach:** **40 States:** The company expanded from operating in just three or four early states (Connecticut, Maryland, Missouri, and California in 2015) to active operations across **40 states**.
* **Market Penetration:** **5% of CMBS Market:** Annual C-PACE issuances currently represent about **5%** of the annual Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities (CMBS) market.
* **Team & Structure:** **Over 100 Employees:** The company employs more than 100 people and maintains an average senior team tenure of **eight years** within an 11-year-old industry.

## Navigating the Commercial Real Estate Crisis
* **The Maturity Wall:** **$1 Trillion Debt Wall:** The commercial real estate market faces a **$1 trillion** maturity wall driven by bank-funded short-term loans requiring balloon payments every 5, 7, or 10 years.
* **Refinancing Gaps:** **Squeezed Proceeds:** Rising interest rates are depressing property values and shrinking operating margins, meaning mortgage proceeds available during refinancing are frequently lower than the original loans from **2021** or **2022**.
* **Risk Mitigation:** **Long-Term Debt Tool:** Borrowers use C-PACE as a risk-mitigation tool to inject equity and secure long-term fixed-rate debt for a portion of their capital stack so they avoid refinancing risks every five years.
* **Sector Agnosticism:** **All Major Asset Classes:** The firm lends across all major asset classes—including office buildings in San Francisco post-COVID and struggling hotels requiring stabilization—by underwriting based on long-term property location and use rather than specific property themes.

## Investor Base & Capital Strategy
* **Primary Lenders:** **Life Insurance Companies:** Capital is sourced primarily from insurance companies, including general account **TIAA-CREF** and international life insurance companies in Asia, due to their appetite for long-dated, secure investments.
* **Exclusion of Private Equity Capital:** **Direct Insurance Execution:** Private equity firms have shown interest in buying the platform, but direct execution with insurance companies remains the best method for providing long-term capital.
* **Historical Milestones:** **2017 Securitization:** Greenworks Lending (founded in **2015**) executed the asset class's first securitization in **2017**, with Nuveen acting as the sole note purchaser before acquiring the company in **2021**.

## Leadership & Organizational Culture
* **Management Philosophy:** **Radical Candor & Psychological Safety:** Ally Cooley applies principles from Kim Scott’s book *Radical Candor*—focusing on psychological safety and knowing team members' backgrounds and career goals—to achieve high staff retention.
* **Parental Transparency:** **Humanizing Leadership:** Cooley openly shares her experiences as a mother of three daughters, modeling work-life trade-offs to foster an open, supportive corporate culture.
* **Nuveen Integration:** **Autonomous Subsidiary:** Despite initial concerns about corporate absorption, Nuveen has maintained a respectful approach to Nuveen Green Capital's investment process and risk management layers while supporting its growth.

## Notable Quotes
> "Green is not in anymore. It's been a rough ride... having that long-term capital is almost the carrot to get them to upgrade their properties to be more energy efficient."
> — Alexandra Cooley

> "Real estate is at its very core, somewhat simple. While rates are going up and operating margins are being squeezed, you just are going to be stuck on proceeds when it comes to refinancing."
> — Alexandra Cooley

> "My mom sells money."
> — Alexandra Cooley's daughter

items.title: Real Estate Investors on Commercial Market Opportunities
items.summary: Despite macroeconomic headwinds like higher construction costs, interest rates, and localized office vacancies, Texas commercial real estate leadership remains overwhelmingly optimistic due to strong underlying fundamentals, accelerating corporate relocation velocity, and massive secular demand for digital and residential infrastructure.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Despite macroeconomic headwinds like higher construction costs, interest rates, and localized office vacancies, Texas commercial real estate leadership remains overwhelmingly optimistic due to strong underlying fundamentals, accelerating corporate relocation velocity, and massive secular demand for digital and residential infrastructure.

## Texas Commercial Market Dynamics & Corporate Migration
* **Shifting Corporate Footprints:** 
  * **Torrey Littlejohn** noted that while Texas recorded 25 corporate headquarters moves this year—the lowest since 2017—the state is experiencing unprecedented velocity in companies establishing new footprints with 50, 100, or 200 employees to test the market before growing exponentially.
  * Companies initially evaluate 3 to 4 submarkets before narrowing down to 1 or 2 ecosystems that seamlessly accommodate both front and back offices.
* **The Urban Core vs. Suburban Barbell:**
  * Downtown Dallas is experiencing positive momentum through residential population growth, new grocery stores, restaurants, and spillover activity from Uptown and the Arts District, despite older, obsolete buildings requiring capital investment.
  * Northern suburbs like Plano and Frisco have developed distinct centers of gravity, creating a balanced "barbell" ecosystem where residents have access to diverse school districts and localized amenities without needing to visit downtown daily.

## Data Centers & Digital Infrastructure
* **The Public Relations vs. Reality Gap:**
  * **Laura Hines-Pierce** described the conversation around data centers and digital infrastructure as overly polarized ("black and white"), noting a critical need for balanced community investment covering housing, social, and physical infrastructure.
  * **Michael Hyun** agreed that data centers have briefly become a "four letter word" in an election year, requiring a pivot toward enhanced community engagement and better-designed, architecturally integrated facilities that avoid looking like landed "Star Wars" ships.
* **Capital Competition & Constraints:**
  * Data center developments are soaking up massive amounts of debt and equity capital, competing with traditional real estate asset classes (like office, retail, and multifamily) as well as long-dated government bonds (with data center bond issuance reaching 68% of long-dated government treasuries over the past year).
  * Data center builds compete directly with traditional real estate for labor and supply, specifically driving up costs for construction contractors.

## Multifamily, Housing, and Residential Master-Planned Communities
* **Multifamily Supply Cycles:**
  * **Michael Hyun** characterized multifamily today as "the office of today"—following the previous retail cycle—driven by oversupply resulting from low interest rates 5 years ago (when 5 and 10-year rates were 350 basis points lower).
  * Multifamily is currently experiencing decade-low starts and supply, with market pain expected to persist for the next 10 to 24 months before returning to equilibrium.
* **Single-Family & Master-Planned Demand:**
  * **Laura Hines-Pierce** highlighted that Hines' highest conviction sector is living/residential, driven by a global under-supply of over 6 million units and a 2025 influx of 400,000 people moving to Texas.
  * Crow Holdings and Hines are actively expanding lot-development platforms nationally (such as Hines' delivery of 50,000 lots) to bridge the gap for homebuilders serving millennials seeking single-family master-planned communities.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Michael Hyun** predicts that multifamily market pain and oversupply distress will last for at least the next 10 to 12 to 24 months before the sector reorganizes.
* **Michael Hyun** predicts that state-level regulatory frameworks for data centers will change to mandate deeper community engagement, noting that while growth may slow down temporarily, Texas will remain a winner in data center CapEx spend due to its business-friendly environment.
* **Michael Hyun** predicts that total state-level bans or halts on data center development will not happen because doing so would be "economic suicide" for the Texas economy.

## Notable Quotes
> "Multifamily today is off is the office of today just like it was here before that. It was retail. And uh, in five years it'll be something else because all of these sectors cycle."
> — **Michael Hyun**

> "Data centers don't need to be a Star Wars ship that has landed in the middle of a community. ... There's an opportunity to deliver a better financial product that leases faster, stays leased longer and gets higher rental rates, but is also an investment in the community."
> — **Laura Hines-Pierce**

> "If there is a significant slowdown in that data center development, that impacts so many areas of the Texas economy... your will then require less natural gas. That will impact the the energy markets, of which Houston and Texas broadly is exposed to."
> — **Michael Hyun**

items.title: TXSE CEO Lee on Listing Standards and New Business
items.summary: The Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) has raised $440 million in total equity backing—including a newly announced investment from State Street—and surpassed $300 billion in listings within its first 22 days of trading.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
The Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) has raised $440 million in total equity backing—including a newly announced investment from State Street—and surpassed $300 billion in listings within its first 22 days of trading. CEO James Lee argues that the 30-year listing duopoly of NYSE and Nasdaq is over, driven by a mission to reduce regulatory and legal frictions for public companies.

## Market Context & The Public Company Decline
- **Shrinking Public Markets:** **James Lee** noted that the U.S. has half the number of public companies it had at its peak 30 years ago (dropping to around 8,100), despite record-high indices.
- **The IPO Backlog:** **James Lee** stated there are currently 31,000 sponsor-backed companies stuck in a heavily backlogged pipeline, representing $4 trillion of marks on sponsors' books. At current exit rates, clearing this backlog will take 9.5 years.
- **Larger Issuance Sizes:** **James Lee** highlighted that today's average IPO market cap at issuance is $2.5 billion—four times larger than 20–23 years ago—meaning everyday investors miss out on the steepest parts of growth curves.
- **Burdensome Disclosures:** **James Lee** contrasted historical prospectuses with modern filings, noting that Anthropic’s recent filing featured a 400-page prospectus with 100 pages dedicated entirely to risk disclosures.

## TXSE Capital, Backing, & Ownership
- **Breaking News - State Street Investment:** **James Lee** announced that State Street has joined TXSE with a significant equity investment, bringing total equity capital to $440 million—an unprecedented amount for an exchange applying for SEC registration.
- **Institutional Backing:** **James Lee** detailed that TXSE’s ownership structure includes BlackRock, Vanguard, JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, and Bank of America.
- **Liquidity Provider Support:** **James Lee** reported that 9 of the top 10 U.S. liquidity providers (representing 90% of daily U.S. equity volume) are equity holders in TXSE.
- **Underwriting & ETF Concentration:** **James Lee** noted that equity holders include lead bookrunners for 91% of IPO proceeds over the last 5 years, and sponsors representing two-thirds of the nation's $17 trillion in ETF assets.

## Exchange Competition & Market Fragmentation
- **End of the Duopoly:** **James Lee** declared that the day of a listing duopoly (Nasdaq and NYSE) is over, establishing TXSE as the third registered listing exchange in the U.S.
- **Trading vs. Listing Disconnect:** **James Lee** addressed concerns about startups lacking track records by explaining that under the National Market System (Reg NMS), there is no longer a correlation between where a company lists and where it trades. Intraday volume for NYSE-listed companies is only 8–9%, with 50% of U.S. volume occurring off-exchange across 20 exchanges and 200 venues.
- **Strict Listing Standards:** **James Lee** emphasized that TXSE has not relaxed standards, adopting quantitative standards higher than its competitors, rendering nearly 35% of current U.S. public corporates ineligible to transfer to TXSE.

## Legal Jurisdictions & Regulatory Alignment
- **The Texas Legal Exodus:** **James Lee** pointed to major companies re-domiciling into Texas—including Tesla, Coinbase, SpaceX, Dillard's, and Exxon (which moved from New Jersey after 144 years on May 27)—creating a viable alternative to Delaware.
- **Quantifiable Cost Reductions:** **James Lee** stated that a standard Fortune 100 company reorganizing into Texas and listing on TXSE can reduce cost structures by tens of millions of dollars annually in insurance savings, franchise taxes, and proxy preparation.
- **Regulatory Tailwinds:** **James Lee** praised current SEC leadership for unravelling reporting apparatus costs, noting the repeal of climate disclosure mandates and the movement to rescind Rule 14a-8 regarding shareholder proposals, aligning with Texas state legislative models like SB 1057.

## Issuer-Aligned Economics
- **Transparent Revenue Sharing:** **James Lee** explained that TXSE’s financial model is entirely issuer-aligned, sharing overall economics (such as market data, corporate actions, and auction revenues) so that public companies experience a net-positive cash relationship rather than just paying opaque listing fees.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Regulatory Timeline:** SEC Chairman Atkins will ring the bell at TXSE on Friday and host a roundtable to discuss state competition and making IPOs great again in America — **James Lee**
- **Upcoming Listings:** Several companies will list on TXSE next week, and the pipeline is full — **James Lee**

## Notable Quotes
> *"The day of a listing duopoly is over. That's ended. And now there are three established listing exchanges in the United States."* — **James Lee**

> *"If you look, uh, despite hitting new highs in the indices... the fact is we have half the number of public companies in this country that we had at the peak at 8,100 public companies 30 years ago."* — **James Lee**

> *"There is no nexus between where you trade and where you list... 90% of your trading volume takes place off exchange."* — **James Lee**

items.title: The AI Boom Will Pull Back, Warns Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler
items.summary: Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler warns that the AI investment boom is a late-stage capital expenditure cycle heading for a deceleration and reversal within 18 to 30 months, with potential financial stability risks tied to over $600 billion in new debt, off-balance-sheet guarantees, and rapid chip obsolescence.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler warns that the AI investment boom is a late-stage capital expenditure cycle heading for a deceleration and reversal within 18 to 30 months, with potential financial stability risks tied to over $600 billion in new debt, off-balance-sheet guarantees, and rapid chip obsolescence.

## AI Boom, Capital Exuberance, and Overbuilding
* **Historical Parallels:** AI investment mirrors past overfunded capital cycles like railroads, canals, and the internet.
  * **Capital Scale:** Companies are raising massive sums, such as Meta's $90 billion equity offering and Broadcom's recent $63 billion package.
  * **Off-Balance-Sheet Risk:** Broadcom, Nvidia, and AMD are utilizing complex guarantees and setting up special purpose vehicles reminiscent of pre-2008 financial structures, sparking concerns similar to the "08 off-balance-sheet craze."
* **Hardware Depreciation:** The heavy funding is concentrated in memory chips and hardware with useful lives of 4 to 7 years. 
  * Due to rapid scaling and technological advances, chips built in 2026 risk losing substantial value by 2032.
* **Productivity vs. Labor Disruptions:** MIT faculty hold diverse views on AI, ranging from expectations of modest productivity gains alongside labor disruptions to optimism about broader productivity gains over the next 5 to 10 years, even amid data center overbuilding.

## Financial Stability and Shadow Debt Risks
* **Insurance Sector Exposure:** Over $500 billion in new debt has been raised this year for AI, pushing near $600 billion when factoring in Broadcom's $63 billion package.
  * **Holding Risk:** The insurance sector has heavily picked up this debt either directly or through private credit.
* **Regulatory Approach:** The U.S. capital markets successfully maintain a merit-neutral stance, allowing public investment in companies like Anthropic provided there are material disclosures of all risks.
* **Central Bank Implications:** The Federal Reserve must factor a potential AI deceleration into future inflation and growth projections for 2027 and 2028.

## Monetary Policy and Macroeconomic Outlook
* **Federal Reserve Path:** Gary Gensler anticipates a rate increase in December, but questions how the Fed will adjust monetary policy afterward if a capex boom deceleration materializes, potentially leading to fewer rate hikes in 2027.
* **Nominal GDP and Fiscal Pressures:** Continuous fiscal stimuli (including the Biden stimulus) risk creating pain and angst as nominal GDP growth is reined in.
* **U.S. vs. France Fiscal Room:** While the U.S. possesses limited fiscal room, it is a larger and more significant economy compared to France, which faces even higher debt-to-economy ratios without the same fiscal room to intervene.

## Politics, Elections, and the Next Two Years
* **Midterms and Presidential Race:** The upcoming midterm elections and early 2028 presidential campaign announcements (potentially starting January or February) will shift political dynamics.
* **Lame-Duck Dynamics:** History indicates presidents in their final two years turn more toward foreign affairs and hold less leverage with Congress.
  * **Bipartisan Priorities:** Democrats gaining leverage in the House or Senate could still collaborate with the executive branch on voter-focused issues, including affordability, housing, AI safety, and youth tech addiction.

## AI and Human Cognition at MIT
* **Student Adoption:** 98% of MIT graduate and undergraduate students use AI regularly, alongside faculty usage.
* **Cognitive Risks:** Humans are biologically wired to conserve energy and avoid exerting their brains, creating a risk of cognitive decline if people offload critical thinking entirely to AI.
* **Critical Thinking:** Success requires treating AI as a constructive bolt-on to critical thinking skills rather than a cognitive crutch.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **AI Deceleration Timeline:** Gary Gensler predicts a deceleration of the AI boom followed by some form of reversal within **18 to 30 months**.
* **Presidential Announcements:** Gary Gensler predicts that 15 to 20 candidates for the 2028 presidential election will announce their runs by **January or February of next year** (or by the Wednesday after the upcoming election).
* **Federal Reserve Rate Actions:** Gary Gensler predicts the Federal Reserve will implement a rate increase in **December**, but may slow or pause rate hikes thereafter as economic deceleration takes hold.

## Notable Quotes
> "I think that we will have, uh, a deceleration of this. I boom and then some form of a reversal in the next 18 to 30 months. And the question really, to me is a little bit about timing when and then how deep it is. And I think the depth of it is going to be all dependent upon all the debt."
> — Gary Gensler

> "When you see the metas raising $90 billion, when you see the debt issuance, which is very significant... You start to worry. Is that's feeling a little like that. Oh eight, uh, off balance sheet craze."
> — Gary Gensler

> "Humans are actually biologically wired to conserve energy. So we're biologically wired not to use our brain as much. And we have to sort of fight against that, that biology and go further."
> — Gary Gensler

items.title: The AI School Kids Love More Than Vacation | Alpha School's Joe Liemandt
items.summary: Driven by cognitive science and large language models (LLMs), Alpha School delivers core academics in just two hours a day—allowing students to learn 10 times faster while spending the rest of their day mastering real-world life skills like teamwork and entrepreneurship.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Driven by cognitive science and large language models (LLMs), Alpha School delivers core academics in just two hours a day—allowing students to learn 10 times faster while spending the rest of their day mastering real-world life skills like teamwork and entrepreneurship. In this discussion, Alpha School Principal Joe Liemandt, a16z podcast host Erik Torenberg, and Horowitz Andreessen Academy (HAA) Co-founder Gagan Biyani explore how this model is being adapted for college-age students to prioritize agency, high-ambition mentorship, and building real-world products over traditional lecture halls.

## Reimagining K-12: The Alpha School Model
* **The 2-Hour Academic Engine:** Traditional schooling methods have stagnated for 100 years. By leveraging modern learning science and LLMs, Alpha has engineered a system where students complete all core academics in **2 hours a day**.
  * **Academic Performance:** Students learn twice as much as they would in a standard 6-to-7-hour school day plus homework, making them top performers on standardized tests.
  * **Precision Engagement:** The learning engine keeps students in an **80 to 85% correct zone**, providing an unending stream of personalized lessons and scaffolding that prevents boredom or burnout.
* **Radical Student Happiness:** By focusing on high standards and challenging group work, 90% of Alpha students report loving school, with **50% overall** (and **65% at one specific campus**) stating they would rather attend school than go on vacation.
* **Rigorous Life Skills Curriculum:** The remainder of the school day is dedicated to five critical life categories: leadership/teamwork, entrepreneurship/financial literacy, socialization/relationship building, public speaking, and grit.
  * **Escape Room Benchmarking:** Third graders are miked up in escape rooms to measure teamwork via AI transcript analysis; students must hit **85% team-oriented language** to graduate the workshop.
  * **Wharton MBA Challenge:** Fourth and fifth graders are required to pass the Wharton MBA simulation challenge (which 50% of adult MBAs fail) as part of their core requirements.
* **Scaling with Quality:** Since taking over as principal 4 years ago, Liemandt has productized the school model, scaling from Austin to **50 campuses** while test scores, student happiness, and workshop quality improve annually.

## Reinventing Higher Education & the HAA Model
* **The Broken University Format:** Speaking to visiting interns from MIT, Stanford, and UT, Liemandt found that **only 1 student out of more than 70** felt their university was properly preparing them for post-graduation life in the age of AI. Large lecture classes have attendance dropping below **10%**, with students viewing them as a charade.
* **Horowitz Andreessen Academy (HAA) Design Principles:** Gagan Biyani explains that HAA applies similar modern principles to college-age students by focusing heavily on student success rather than adult politics.
  * **The 80-Hour Internship Test:** Summer interns at Alpha worked 80 hours a week researching learning science and building educational small language models (SLMs) to make them free for global sovereigns, proving that motivated students thrive when building real products.
  * **High-Ambition Travel and Autonomy:** HAA allocates **$5,000 per student** for travel budgets, encouraging solo travel to countries with less than **$20,000 GDP per capita** to build global perspective and resilience.
* **The Value of Network and Proximity:** Drawing inspiration from early institutions like the Teal Fellowship, HAA curates its applicant pool tightly, exposing students to legendary builders (such as Jensen Huang, Sam Altman, and Satya Nadella) to raise their personal ambitions.

## Entrepreneurship and the Future of Work
* **Founder School:** Alpha launched a specialized high school focused entirely on entrepreneurship, recognizing that AI will drive a massive explosion in independent business creation.
* **The Million-Dollar Guarantee:** Founder School guarantees that students will start a business earning **$1 million in profit** while in high school, or tuition is refunded. Students are currently speed-running the curriculum as freshmen.
* **The Power of Cold Outreach:** Highlighting student agency, Liemandt shared the story of a 14-year-old student who cold-called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. While Huang critiqued the student's call preparation (giving him an "F" on research), he took the call and gave him mentorship—turning it into a transformative life lesson.

## Overcoming Parental Resistance and Cultural Inertia
* **The 1910 Farm Tractor Analogy:** Liemandt compares the current educational inflection point to 1910, when the introduction of the farm tractor made 30% of agricultural jobs obsolete, prompting 130,000 American towns to vote to raise taxes to fund a brand-new high school system.
* **Adoption Curves:** Opening new campuses often starts with small cohorts (e.g., opening New York City with **10 to 12 students**), but demand skyrockets once local families witness the actual performance and happiness of the first cohorts.
* **Product Definition:** Liemandt stresses that schools must clearly define their product—attracting families who embrace modern tools and repelling laggards who reject screens or AI.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Are you willing to redesign your school day so kids love it more than vacation? With cognitive science and learning science, plus the advent of LLMs, you can build a learning engine that teaches kids 10 times faster."* — **Joe Liemandt**

> *"If you actually listen to Joe talk... K-8, high school, very different when you go from high school to college era... If you just told the leaders of any major university in the country that their number one job and no other job was to make sure that the students were succeeding, I'm sure that there would be many great schools... unfortunately, there aren't many."* — **Gagan Biyani**

> *"The key to your child's happiness is high standards. Kids want to do hard things, right? They love to do hard things and they love to do hard things with their friends."* — **Joe Liemandt**

> *"The question of what field should I study so that I can be sure that I'm resilient to the future is not the right question. The question is what field am I interested in? I think there's enough faith that if you're AI-native in any field, it does not matter."* — **Gagan Biyani**

items.title: The airline CEO putting Starlink on every plane
items.summary: Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines, details the airline’s contrarian pandemic strategy of massive fleet and technology expansion, the rollout of SpaceX Starlink across every plane, and why customer surveys and traditional metrics fail in the airline business.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines, details the airline’s contrarian pandemic strategy of massive fleet and technology expansion, the rollout of SpaceX Starlink across every plane, and why customer surveys and traditional metrics fail in the airline business.

## Fleet Expansion & Contrarian Bets
* **Pandemic Wide-Body Order:** During COVID when travel experts predicted demand would drop 50% forever and global competitors permanently retired wide-body fleets, Scott Kirby and United did the opposite, executing the largest aircraft order in history: 200 wide-bodies and several hundred narrow-bodies.
* **Capital Discipline vs. Short-Termism:** United invested heavily during the downturn to secure 30-year assets at advantageous pricing, mirroring cyclical manufacturing strategies like Samsung's memory investments.
* **Market Dominance in Hubs:** Scott Kirby highlights that single-hub operations (like Atlanta and Dallas) drive more international service and economic activity than fragmented hubs like Chicago, where United and American Airlines duplicate 16 daily flights to Milwaukee.

## Technology Stack & In-House Software
* **Core Tech Modernization:** In 2020, United invested hundreds of millions to move off mainframes onto the cloud and build modern databases, enabling fast execution that competitors cannot replicate.
* **In-House Reservation Legacy:** United is one of only two airlines globally (alongside Copa Airlines) that owns its own reservation system, refusing to outsource to Sabre or Apollo.
* **Seat-Back Map & Entertainment Redesign:** United is taking over map software from Panasonic to eliminate annoying globe views and build personalized preferences and proactive milestone memories (such as a live countdown to a passenger's 2 millionth mile).
* **AI Vibe Coding:** After taking three 1-hour tutoring sessions, Scott Kirby independently wrote a sports betting aggregation web app in 2.5 hours at his home gym, sparking an internal AI push.

## Starlink Rollout & Competitive Differentiation
* **Speed Over "Free":** United chose SpaceX's Starlink not because it is free, but because fast bandwidth is the true value proposition; legacy free Wi-Fi is compared to slow dial-up internet.
* **Fleet Rollout Pace:** United is currently at 48% of flights equipped with Starlink, upgrading about three planes per day and planning to reach 50% within a week and 100% in hubs like Los Angeles in the first half of next year.
* **Targeting Competitors:** Scott Kirby views Starlink as a temporary multi-year competitive advantage that will drive passengers from competing airlines (including Delta and joint-venture partner ANA) to try United and stay for its superior overall technology.

## Operational Hurdles & Air Traffic Control
* **ATC as the Primary Bottleneck:** Air traffic control accounts for 90% of airline operational issues, constrained by inefficient annual appropriations processes and political distribution of 450 regional facilities.
* **Weather Simulation:** United is using AI simulations for Denver summer pop-up thunderstorms to potentially reduce weather-impacted delays by 50%–75%.
* **Low-Cost Carrier Failures:** Low-cost carriers like Spirit Airlines failed because cost inflation and exorbitant airport authority fees (such as $52 per passenger in New York airports) made their business model mathematically unsustainable.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Hub-Specific Starlink Target:** Scott Kirby stated that Los Angeles will be United's first 100% Starlink-equipped hub in the first half of next year.
* **Weather Delay Reductions:** Scott Kirby claimed that AI simulations can reduce weather-impacted delays in Denver by 50% to 75% in the summer.
* **Industry Financial Outlook:** Scott Kirby predicted that 6 out of 10 US airlines will lose money this year.

## Notable Quotes
> "The experts live in the world of two standard deviations. They force-fit everything into the things that they've already seen. When things happen outside two standard deviations, when the tails happen, which is where you create all the value… That's where I first started."
> — Scott Kirby

> "Anyone that says the word weather in my presence is going to get fired, because I do not want to use weather as an excuse. I know weather happens... but our job is to figure out how to minimize the impact of weather."
> — Scott Kirby

> "Our constraint on investing in technology is how much can we manage? It is not money."
> — Scott Kirby

items.title: Traders Brace for Fed Day
items.summary: Global equity markets are led by a tech rally and heavy upcoming earnings as the Federal Reserve begins a two-day policy meeting amid a complex economic landscape.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Global equity markets are led by a tech rally and heavy upcoming earnings as the Federal Reserve begins a two-day policy meeting amid a complex economic landscape. Concurrently, high-stakes national elections are underway in Israel, and corporate leaders and athletes discuss shifting market dynamics across real estate, supply chains, and endurance sports.

## Markets, Fed Policy & Macroeconomic Complexity
* **Federal Reserve Meeting:** The Fed kicked off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, with interest rate decisions and a press conference led by Chairman Kevin Warsh anticipated 24 hours later. Central banks in the Eurozone and Japan are also expected to keep rates steady.
* **U.S. Economy Analysis:** Bloomberg's Enda Curran describes the current environment as exceptionally confusing due to contradictory indicators, including a frozen housing market alongside high prices, soaring bond yields with record stock market highs, and strong GDP growth and corporate profits contrasted with struggling lower-income workers and elevated costs.
* **Inflation Pressures:** September inflation figures revealed broad-based price pressures, including record increases in toy prices potentially impacted by tariffs, alongside energy spillover risks affecting diesel and food delivery costs.
* **Market Performance:** The S&P 500 rose 42 points (0.5%) to 7,718, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.2%, the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.1%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) surged 3.3%. The Dow fell 4 points. Spot gold increased 1% to $4,058/oz, WTI crude dropped 1.9% to $99.83/barrel, and Brent crude fell 1.8% to $113.73/barrel. Yields stood at 4.73% for the 2-year, 4.99% for the 10-year, and 5.30% for the 30-year.

## Global Politics: Israel National Elections
* **Referendum on Netanyahu:** Voting closes in Israel's first national election since the October 7th attack, serving as a high-turnout referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political career. 
* **Political Landscape & Coalition Dynamics:** Bloomberg Israel Bureau Chief Ethan Bronner reports a razor-thin race between Netanyahu's bloc (allied with ultra-orthodox and national religious parties) and the center-right opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot. No party wins an outright majority, requiring post-election coalition horse-trading to reach a 61-seat threshold.
* **Policy Differences:** While security and troop deployments in regional conflicts will remain largely unchanged, an opposition win could see a crackdown on settler violence, a more deliberate and limited approach regarding Iran (avoiding regime change), greater transparency, and repaired U.S. relations.
* **Economic & Legal Impacts:** The Israeli economy has shown resilience, but faces major drags including a high-earning brain drain and heavy defense spending. Netanyahu's ongoing trial on bribery, fraud, and breach of trust charges will proceed, carrying potential prison time if he loses power.

## Alternative Real Estate, Senior Housing & Data Centers
* **Harrison Street Asset Management Strategy:** Global CEO Chris Merrill highlighted a focus on need-based, essential services and social infrastructure that perform across economic cycles.
* **Senior Housing Demographics:** The firm targets the aging population—noting nearly 2 million people turning 80 annually and high post-85 memory care needs—focusing on private-pay, rental-based continuums of care (independent, assisted, memory care) across 35 to 40 states.
* **Data Center Expansion:** Data center demand is "off the charts," but growth is severely constrained by access to power. Harrison Street manages risk via long-term net leases with hyper-scale tenants and essential off-takers (universities, health systems) in high-power nodes like Northern Virginia.
* **Capital Return & Sales:** The firm anticipates selling $6 billion to $7 billion in assets this year, prioritizing DPI (Distributed to Paid-In capital) as a core metric to return capital to investors amid strong buyer demand for non-traditional alternative segments.

## Sports & Endurance: The Eliud Kipchoge World Tour
* **World Tour Mission:** Two-time Olympic marathon gold medalist and Nike partner Eliud Kipchoge discussed his multi-year world tour running marathons across all seven continents over the next two years to spread the spirit of running, unity, and health.
* **Philosophy & Mental Resilience:** Kipchoge emphasized his guiding principle that "no human is limited," asserting that perceived barriers exist purely in the mind and apply to any profession (engineering, medicine, law). He cited breaking the two-hour marathon barrier as his toughest mental hurdle, overcome through trust in himself and his team.
* **Nutrition & Gear Evolution:** Kipchoge highlighted structured fueling every 5 kilometers as a game-changer for marathon recovery and energy. He credited ongoing technological advancements in Nike footwear—focused on muscle stability and rapid recovery—as key drivers of endurance sport progression.

## Public Markets & Capital Formation
* **TXSE Group Perspective:** At Bloomberg Invest Dallas, TXSE Group Chairman and CEO James Lee discussed the backlog of sponsor-backed companies (31,000 companies and $4 trillion in marks) and argued that a listing duopoly and overly burdensome public market regulations have forced companies to stay private much longer.
* **Stock Movers (Tatiana Darie):** 
  * **Boeing (BA):** Shares dropped 10% (the largest drop since the April tariff tantrum) after lowering full-year delivery targets for 737 MAX jets due to wing manufacturing and engine delivery challenges.
  * **Hilton (HLT):** Shares fell 2% despite a top-and-bottom-line beat and strong U.S./European demand (RevPAR up 7%), driven by EPS guidance falling short of estimates and weakness in the Middle East and China.
  * **UPS (UPS):** Shares gained 5% following a beat-and-raise quarter driven by higher pricing, resilient domestic volume, and the winding down of headwinds related to former primary customer Amazon.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Ethan Bronner:** Predicting that election outcomes will take weeks to fully shake out rather than being known immediately, and that the trial of Benjamin Netanyahu will likely continue for several years through appeals.
* **Chris Merrill:** Asserting that Harrison Street will sell $6 billion to $7 billion in assets this year.

## Notable Quotes
> "Everyone has a different story on it. It is a strong economy, but the, I think the unifying narrative among everyone, household and and business, is that costs are high and they're increasing."
> — **Enda Curran**

> "If the opposition were to win, we would expect less money going to war, and the likelihood that people would stop leaving so much and maybe start to come back."
> — **Ethan Bronner**

> "When you think about demographics, I mean, look what's happening in healthcare and the aging population. I mean, we really are staring at a wall and a huge number of people turning 80, almost 2 million every year."
> — **Chris Merrill**

> "Running actually is the road. But the main reason, are the people to make sure I I sell the spirit of running... to tell people that running brings unity, brings togetherness, and about power pole, it's healthy."
> — **Eliud Kipchoge**

items.title: UPS CEO Carol Tomé Talks Company Growth | Bloomberg Talks
items.summary: UPS reported solid third-quarter results with a return to U.S. volume growth, enabling the company to raise its full-year guidance and project profit and margin expansion heading into 2027 through disciplined, precision growth.
items.content_text:
- **TL;DR:** UPS reported solid third-quarter results with a return to U.S. volume growth, enabling the company to raise its full-year guidance and project profit and margin expansion heading into 2027 through disciplined, precision growth.

## Q3 Financial Results & 2027 Growth Outlook
- **Solid Third-Quarter Performance:** UPS beat several financial metrics and raised its full-year revenue and profit guidance following a return to volume growth among U.S. small-business (SMB) and enterprise customers. (Carol Tomé)
- **Holiday Peak Forecasts:** Based on customer forecasts, average daily volume is expected to jump approximately 25% from the third quarter to the fourth quarter during the peak holiday season. (Carol Tomé)
- **The 2027 Growth Formula:** Management outlined an "algebraic formula" for 2027 featuring volume growth and revenue-per-piece (RPP) growth outpacing cost-per-piece (CPP) growth, driving profit and margin expansion. (Carol Tomé)
- **Cost vs. Revenue Dynamics:** 
  - Domestically, revenue per piece grew 6.1% compared to a 5.5% increase in cost per piece. (Romaine Bostick / Carol Tomé)
  - Higher fuel costs and purchased-transportation expenses drove 100% of the cost-per-piece growth. (Carol Tomé)
  - Fuel surcharges accounted for roughly half of the RPP increase, while base rates and mix drove the other half. (Carol Tomé / Romaine Bostick)
  - The expected long-term gap between RPP and CPP growth is projected to range between 50 and 100 basis points. (Carol Tomé)

## Network Transformation & "Precision Growth"
- **Dispelling Volume Myths:** UPS is moving away from the belief that "all packages are created equal" and that volume solves all problems, opting instead for a leaner, more efficient network. (Carol Tomé)
- **Post-Amazon Pivot:** 
  - The plan initiated in early 2025 to reduce Amazon's share of UPS business is largely complete, positioning the company for a post-Amazon era of automated, efficient network growth. (Carol Tomé / Romaine Bostick)
  - The total addressable market is estimated at $923 billion from factory floor to front door, with the premium space valued at $535 billion globally and $150 billion in the U.S. (Carol Tomé)
- **Organizational Restructuring:** 
  - UPS recently reorganized to eliminate dual standards between U.S. and international operations, placing Nando Cesarone in charge of global operations to unify standards, automation, and service-level agreements. (Carol Tomé)
  - The company appointed two experienced P&L leaders to run the U.S. business and international healthcare/supply chain divisions. (Carol Tomé)

## Healthcare & Supply Chain Logistics Expansion
- **Complex Healthcare Leadership:** 
  - UPS has positioned itself as the global leader in complex healthcare logistics, with healthcare revenue projected to exceed $13 billion by the end of the year (up from under $6 billion six years ago). (Carol Tomé)
  - Assets include over 20 million square feet of dedicated healthcare logistics space across 273 buildings in 36 countries, featuring cold-chain capabilities, special labeling, and control towers. (Carol Tomé)
  - Profit margins in the healthcare delivery business sit in the low-to-mid teens. (Carol Tomé)
  - The global addressable market for complex healthcare logistics is approximately $90 billion, bolstered by direct-to-home pharmaceutical delivery for GLP-1 drugs. (Carol Tomé)
  - Authority in this space was earned during the pandemic by delivering 1 billion COVID-19 vaccines in the first year with 99.9% effectiveness and zero temperature excursions. (Carol Tomé)
- **Supply Chain Solutions & Forwarding:** 
  - The forwarding and logistics business saw 17% growth in the quarter, driven primarily by premium healthcare and data center construction. (Carol Tomé)
  - Data center construction materials imported from outside the U.S., warehoused, and delivered represent an addressable logistics market of over $15 billion. (Carol Tomé)

## Technology, Productivity & Labor Relations
- **Sensing vs. Scanning:** 
  - RFID sensing technology is being deployed across package cars, replacing manual loader scanning to eliminate misloads and drive unprecedented productivity. (Carol Tomé)
  - Productivity improvements are viewed as a continuous, virtuous cycle running through 2027 and beyond. (Carol Tomé)
- **Labor Strategy & Teamster Relations:** 
  - Part-time building roles experience high student turnover, which absorbs automation naturally without backfilling. (Carol Tomé)
  - Package drivers are the "brand people" and face of UPS, with leadership expressing no desire to automate or introduce autonomy to their roles. (Carol Tomé)
  - Carol Tomé plans to remain CEO through the negotiation of the next Teamsters contract, which expires on August 1, 2028, making her only the second CEO in company history (aside from the founder) to negotiate two union contracts. (Carol Tomé / Romaine Bostick)
  - Management noted lessons learned from the 2023 negotiations—specifically committing to being "very clear" on achieving a "win-win-win" desired outcome. (Carol Tomé)

## Global Trade & Macro Trends
- **Trade Lane Dynamics:** 
  - Inbound trade into the U.S. turned positive at the end of the quarter. (Carol Tomé)
  - Asia-to-Asia trade lanes grew over 8% during the quarter. (Carol Tomé)
  - Europe experienced a significant trade drop following the elimination of the de minimis exemption in July, though it is beginning to recover. (Carol Tomé)
  - Canadian border activity shows mild softness, which management characterizes as cyclical rather than structural. (Carol Tomé)

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Average Daily Volume Increase:** Average daily volume is expected to rise about 25% from the third quarter to the fourth quarter during the holiday peak, based on customer forecasts. — Carol Tomé
- **Revenue Per Piece vs. Cost Per Piece Gap:** The gap between revenue-per-piece (RPP) and cost-per-piece (CPP) growth will range between 50 and 100 basis points. — Carol Tomé
- **Healthcare Addressable Market:** The addressable market for complex healthcare logistics globally is approximately $90 billion. — Carol Tomé
- **Data Center Logistics Addressable Market:** The logistics and supply chain opportunity for data center build-outs in the United States is over $15 billion. — Carol Tomé
- **CEO Tenure & Contract Timeline:** Carol Tomé is committed to staying through the end of her current turnaround mandate and negotiating the next Teamster contract, which expires on August 1, 2028. — Carol Tomé

## Notable Quotes
> "Instead, we looked at our end-to-end network, our global smart integrated network, and said, okay, who can we serve best and serve them better than anybody else? And we’ve determined, it’s not a lightweight short-zone box of sweaters, it’s actually complex logistics like complex healthcare..."
> — Carol Tomé

> "Precision growth. This is a big, important value, um, equation, precision growth. We want to be selective, focused, and balanced, grow in the right parts of the market, serve our customers better than anybody else, and create a whole lot of money doing that."
> — Carol Tomé

> "In 2023 we said that our desired outcome was win-win-win. [...] In 2028, we’ll be very clear on what our desired outcome is."
> — Carol Tomé

items.title: Washington Today (10-27-26):  Pres. Trump says he will respect midterm results 'if they are honest'
items.summary: President Trump stated he will respect the upcoming midterm results if they are honest while campaigning in Texas amid a tightly contested political landscape.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
President Trump stated he will respect the upcoming midterm results if they are honest while campaigning in Texas amid a tightly contested political landscape. Meanwhile, voters head to the polls in high-stakes congressional races across the nation, an election in Israel, and high-profile legal and political flashpoints.

## Midterm Elections & National Political Landscape
* **National Polling and Favorability:** 
  * An NPR/PBS News/Marist poll released Tuesday showed Democrats holding an 8-point advantage (52% to 44%) over Republicans heading into the final week before the midterms.
* **President Trump's Campaign & Statements:** 
  * President Donald Trump campaigned in Texas at rallies in Corpus Christi and Lubbock, supporting candidates including U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton and viewing Venezuelan oil shipments in Port Arthur alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
  * Trump stated he would work with Democrats if they win congressional majorities and will respect the midterm results "if they are honest elections."
* **House Leadership Commitments:** 
  * U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-LA), while campaigning with Rep. Mike Lawler in Orangeburg, New York, dismissed doomsday scenarios regarding transferring power, affirming he is a constitutional law attorney who will follow the Constitution to seat winning members on January 3rd.

## Texas Senate & Congressional Races
* **Paxton vs. Talarico Senate Race:** 
  * Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic state Representative James Talarico have been tied in polls for months in a remarkably competitive Texas Senate race.
  * Trump criticized Talarico over cultural issues and policies, while Talarico targeted Paxton over ties to wealthy donors like Elon Musk, campaign spending, and corporate PAC influence.
* **House Redistricting Outlook:** 
  * Associated Press Washington Correspondent Steven Sloan noted that Republican redistricting efforts to gain five U.S. House seats may fall short if the national environment proves heavily favorable to Democrats, threatening the GOP's slim 4-seat House majority.

## Michigan Senate & House Dynamics
* **Vance Rally for Rogers:** 
  * Vice President J.D. Vance rallied in Howell, Michigan, supporting Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers against Democratic opponent Abdul El-Sayed.
* **Gongwer Expert Insights:** 
  * Alethia Kasbin and Zach Gorchow noted on C-SPAN that Michigan is a closely divided purple state (splitting identifiers evenly near 40% per party with 20% independent) where Republicans historically struggle to match Donald Trump's turnout levels down-ballot.

## Key Congressional & State Battles (Maine and New York)
* **Maine's Second District:** 
  * Former Republican Governor Paul LePage accused opponent Matt Dunlap of failing to address government benefit and program fraud during a campaign stop in Lewiston, Maine.
  * Independent Senator Angus King endorsed Democrat Matt Dunlap, whose race against LePage is rated a competitive underdog fight in a district won three times by Donald Trump.
* **New York's 17th District:** 
  * Republican incumbent Rep. Mike Lawler held a news conference criticizing Democratic challenger Kate Connelly as a "carpetbagger" with ties to Virginia.
  * Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD) campaigned for Connelly in a Cook Political Report toss-up race held in a district that voted for Kamala Harris in 2024.

## Immigration Enforcement & Justice Department Controversies
* **Alex Preddy Family Appeal:** 
  * Michael and Susan Preddy, parents of Alex Preddy (who was shot and killed by federal immigration agents during Minneapolis's "Operation Metro Surge"), held their first news conference calling on the Justice Department to prosecute those responsible and clear their son's name.
* **House Minority Leader Push:** 
  * House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called for cutting off all funding to ICE during a Houston labor union meeting, criticizing immigration enforcement sweeps and demanding judicial warrants and local accountability.

## International Updates: Israel & Ukraine
* **Israel Election Day:** 
  * Voters in Israel cast ballots in parliamentary elections for the first time since the Hamas attack three years ago, with exit polls showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and opposition rivals falling short of an outright 61-seat majority, leaving Arab parties potentially positioned as kingmakers.
* **Ukraine Localized Ceasefire:** 
  * Russia and Ukraine observed a localized ceasefire in a southern Ukrainian city ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump.

## Notable Quotes
> "I'll respect the results whatever happens? I will, if they're honest elections, deal."
> — President Donald Trump

> "We have a little ship, see that little ship out there? That's got 1 million barrels of oil on it from Venezuela. And we're celebrating the greatest oil victory in history."
> — President Donald Trump

> "All we want is justice for Alex... We are not asking for any special treatment. We do not want to be on TV, we are not political activists... All we want is justice for Alex."
> — Susan Preddy

items.title: Wells Fargo, UBS & Citi on Servicing the Texas Wealthy
items.summary: North Texas has experienced a doubling of wealth over the past decade, driven by a massive influx of people, corporate headquarters, and a resilient entrepreneurial culture, even as wealth managers navigate the human complexities of the great wealth transfer and AI integration.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
North Texas has experienced a doubling of wealth over the past decade, driven by a massive influx of people, corporate headquarters, and a resilient entrepreneurial culture, even as wealth managers navigate the human complexities of the great wealth transfer and AI integration.

## The North Texas Wealth Boom & Influx
- **Population & Economic Inflow:** Approximately 900,000 people have moved to Texas in the last five years, contributing to a diverse economy spanning energy, tech, healthcare, commercial real estate, and finance (Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo; William Thompson, UBS; Clinton Warren, Citi).
- **Corporate Relocations:** Major companies have established global headquarters in the region, such as Charles Schwab near Westlake and Fidelity Investments, alongside a massive wave of real estate development in western suburbs (William Thompson, UBS).
- **Cross-Industry Collaboration:** New arrivals are networking and doing deals across traditional and emerging sectors, bolstered by networks and venture capital initiatives built by figures like Ross Perot and Aaron Pierce (Clinton Warren, Citi).

## Alternative Investments, Real Estate, and AI Exposure
- **Private Markets & Democratization:** Ultra-high-net-worth investors and family offices remain heavily committed to private markets, looking for liquidity and deal opportunities without any slowdown in commitment (William Thompson, UBS).
- **Private Credit Compression:** An influx of capital chasing private credit deals has caused expected yields to compress, with interest rates dropping from 15% down to 9% or 10% in some cases (William Thompson, UBS).
- **Data Center & Land Transactions:** Massive valuations and eye-watering offers—driven by AI infrastructure and data center development (including projects tied to Elon Musk)—are prompting multi-generational ranch-owning families to sell land they never expected to part with (William Thompson, UBS).
- **AI Portfolio Diligence:** While major IPOs like Anthropic draw interest, advisors stress that investors must audit their portfolios to understand their actual AI exposure and avoid repeating historical valuation bubbles like the .com era (Clinton Warren, Citi; William Thompson, UBS).

## Generational Wealth Transfer & Family Dynamics
- **Misaligned Inheritances:** According to wealth studies, 67% of business-owning parents do not anticipate leaving their businesses to their children, creating a disconnect with kids who assume they will inherit them (Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo).
- **Entrepreneurial Next-Gen:** Millennials and Gen Z heirs are showing high entrepreneurial spirits, often seeking capital to start new businesses or repurpose legacy assets—such as converting ranch lands into new ventures (Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo).
- **The Role of Human Advisors:** As multi-generational family goals splinter and asset legacy meanings shift, the core value of wealth managers increasingly relies on navigating complex family psychology and human "sticky muck" rather than commoditized portfolio management (Clinton Warren, Citi; Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo).

## Technology & Election Impact on Wealth Management
- **AI in Investment Committees:** Some large family offices are experimenting with unconventional governance, such as replacing a human investment committee member with an AI agent to vote on cash flows, capital calls, and exposures (Clinton Warren, Citi).
- **The Human Element in Advisory:** Despite clients experimenting with AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude for financial questions, zero advisors reported clients challenging them without human advisory backing; firms are leaning into high-touch human elements (Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo).
- **Election and Policy Sentiments:** While clients frequently inquire about portfolio hedging during election cycles, wholesale liquidation is rare due to tax consequences; investors are primarily focused on practical risk management, interest rate trajectories, and potential regulatory shifts concerning AI and energy (Clinton Warren, Citi; William Thompson, UBS; Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo).

## Notable Quotes
> "People are routed with we're going to support each other if we're all here to grow the pie. So if you're willing to get your boots dirty, you're going to roll up your sleeves, you're going to work hard and you're growing the pie..."
> — **Clinton Warren, Citi**

> "Our business is going to have to continue to become an increasingly human business and a business that gets to the pieces that a robot is never, ever, ever going to do... That's where you separate yourself... is being able to get into that, the sticky muck of humanity."
> — **Heather Hunt-Ruddy, Wells Fargo**

> "No matter which one, pick one. We get a lot of conversation or get a lot of inquiries about portfolio hedging because large investors are generally not going to wholesale their portfolio and accept tax consequences just to, you know, hide in a hide under, you know, under a rock for a while."
> — **William Thompson, UBS**
